source_title: WHO FAO Food safety is everyone’s business in street food vending
direct_observation: An estimated 2.5 billion people eat street food daily; it provides inexpensive convenient sometimes nutritious food and income especially for women while carrying food-safety risk
missing_stage: named household affordability nutrition illness and vendor income
evidence_status: high for global mechanism; medium for outcomes
next_test: follow one corridor consumers vendors and food-safety incidents

source_title: FAO food supply and distribution indicator
unit_or_scope: informal food systems and connected formal chains
direct_observation: Informal production processing transport and retail contribute to food security and connect with formal firms; unsafe food can damage confidence and incomes across the chain
missing_stage: named supply price safety and continuity outcomes
evidence_status: high for architecture; medium for local effects
next_test: map one vendor chain from producer to household purchase

source_title: WHO traditional food markets and Indonesia Five Keys pilot
unit_or_scope: traditional markets in Asia and Indonesia pilot sites
direct_observation: Traditional markets are economic cultural social and livelihood institutions; pilot identified water quality cleaning pest and animal-handling gaps while working with market workers
missing_stage: foodborne illness price vendor income and post-pilot maintenance
evidence_status: high for framework; medium for effects
next_test: compare market hygiene infrastructure and incident records before/after

source_title: ILO The informal economy and street vendors
unit_or_scope: urban informal workers and public-space governance
direct_observation: Street vendors provide jobs low-cost goods and urban culture but face weak services social security eviction confiscation bribery and regulatory conflict
missing_stage: formalisation fee income voice safety and social protection
evidence_status: high for mechanism; medium for named outcomes
next_test: follow vendor group through licence relocation and one enforcement cycle

source_title: WHO mitigating risks in traditional food markets
unit_or_scope: urban and rural traditional markets Asia Pacific
direct_observation: Five Keys address cleanliness contamination product safety animal contact and personal protection; markets can be major livelihood and food-security institutions but unsafe if unmanaged
missing_stage: consumer access cultural continuity worker outcomes and durable compliance
evidence_status: high for framework; medium for closure
next_test: build a named market ledger with water waste inspection and user outcomes

source_title: WHO Indonesia risk-based food inspection pilot
unit_or_scope: 159 Puskesmas and 3681 food vendors across five districts or municipalities
direct_observation: Risk calculator assessed food profile mitigation business size and inspection discrepancies; 3681 vendors were assessed and sanitarian knowledge rose from 60% to 76%
closed_stage: risk-based inspection architecture and workforce capability
missing_stage: foodborne illness vendor cost affordability appeal corruption and durable compliance
evidence_status: high for operating mechanism; low for consumer and livelihood outcomes
next_test: follow sampled high medium and low-risk vendors through inspection correction cost and consumer incident records

source_title: WHO Indonesia Five Keys traditional-market pilot
unit_or_scope: three locations in Semarang Bandung and Samarinda
direct_observation: Vendor hygiene knowledge rose from 84% to 90% and reported kiosk or floor cleaning with water and soap or disinfectant rose from 70% to 80%; gaps included water assessment cleaning protocols pests and live-animal handling
closed_stage: practice-level hygiene change and market-community engagement
missing_stage: foodborne illness zoonosis price income women control customer access and maintenance
evidence_status: medium for practice change; low for health and livelihood outcomes
next_test: repeat objective inspection and illness price income and vendor-retention measures after 6 12 and 24 months

source_title: FAO Central Accra street-food vendor survey
stage: gendered spatial food-access and livelihood mechanism
direct_observation: Vendors were almost all women; nearly half operated near schools; the activity was concentrated in poverty-pocket areas and reported acceptable sample hygiene and safety
closed_stage: vendor geography gender and school-food access mechanism
missing_stage: dietary adequacy child health profit control of earnings causal school effects and post-policy change
evidence_status: medium for mechanism; low for causal outcomes
next_test: follow vendor earnings women decision power student purchases diet and illness by school corridor

source_title: UN-Habitat Pasto Urban Resilience Action Plan
unit_or_scope: El Potrerillo market and surrounding Pasto watersheds
direct_observation: El Potrerillo is identified as a critical hub for local livelihoods and food security; the plan includes informal workers market actors community organisations universities and institutions
missing_stage: shock continuity price income infrastructure performance and binding worker decision rights
evidence_status: medium for planning signal; low for delivered outcomes
next_test: track one climate or flood shock through market supply prices vendor continuity and participation decisions
